title: Family and home
intro: Let's go home for a bit. Genii promises not to ask about your grades. Mostly.

cards.prompt: Someday: week one in your own place with your person or a roommate. The sink is full, the trash smells, and you're both just staring at it.

options.t: Copy my family's system. It worked for years.
Split by what we each hate least. I'll take trash.
Make a chore wheel and spin it every week.
Pay a cleaner, split the bill, never fight about it.

cards.mask: looks like a chore standoff; measures whether a home runs on the inherited script or one you write from scratch (R3, T20)

friend.prompt: {name} moves in with someone. The sink is full and nobody moves. What does {name} do?

a.t: Sets it up the way {name}'s family always did.

b.t: Splits chores by what each of them hates least.

cards.prompt: Think of the last time your family pushed back hard on a plan of yours: a trip, a school, a move, a haircut.

options.t: Did it anyway. Told them after it went fine.
Talked it through, dinner after dinner, until they came around.
Dropped it. Peace at home was worth more.
Heard them out, then picked my own timing.
Went with theirs. Their money, their rules.

cards.mask: looks like a family argument story; measures whether your big calls are made together or by you (R1, T19)

friend.prompt: {name}'s family pushes back hard on a plan. What does {name} do?

a.t: Talks it through until the family is on board.

b.t: Listens, then decides the timing alone.

cards.prompt: A couple you know swapped the expected setup: the one everyone assumed would stay home works, and the other raises the kids. For your own home?

options.t: Same energy. I'd run mine that way too.
Love it for them. Mine would run classic.

cards.mask: looks like an opinion on another family; measures whether the new script is fine for others but not for you (R3, T20A split)

friend.prompt: A couple swaps who works and who stays home. Would {name} set up a home that way?

b.t: Love it for them, classic for {name}.

cards.prompt: A parent needs daily care for the next six months. Your siblings could help. Moving back home would cost you at work.
cards.teenPrompt: A grandparent moves in and needs daily help for a few months. Your family asks who can pitch in after school.

options.t: Say 'I've got it' before anyone else can answer.
Start a shared calendar. Everyone takes shifts.
Look up outside help and pitch it at dinner.
Wait to see who steps up, then fill the gaps.
Nobody else can. It lands on me either way.

cards.mask: looks like a logistics problem; measures whether you carry family need yourself or build a shared system around it (T18)

friend.prompt: Someone in {name}'s family needs daily care for months. What does {name} do first?

a.t: Says 'I've got it' before anyone else answers.

b.t: Starts a shared schedule so everyone takes shifts.

cards.prompt: That care question. What showed up first?

options.t: Guilt, for even hesitating.
Worry. About them, not the schedule.
A tiny voice asking, 'Why is it always me?'
Warmth. This is what family is for.
Relief that I'm not an only child.

cards.mask: looks like a check-in; measures the emotion under family duty (research record and tag copy only, no profile evidence)

cards.prompt: Your parents offer to help you get your own place. One catch: it has to be a ten-minute walk from theirs.
cards.teenPrompt: Someday, your parents offer to help pay for your first apartment. One catch: it has to be a ten-minute walk from theirs.

options.t: Deal. Free help and home-cooked dinners nearby.
Only if that area was already on my list.
Say no. I'll find my own place, even if later.
Depends on how often 'nearby' means 'dropping by'.
Couldn't do it without their help anyway.

options: If they'd drop by without asking
If the area works for my school or job
If the help came with more strings later

cards.mask: looks like a housing perk; measures whether family help with family hopes feels like closeness or like a leash (R1, T19)

friend.prompt: {name}'s parents will help with a place, if it's a ten-minute walk from theirs. {name}…

a.t: Takes it. Close to family is a bonus.

b.t: Says no unless the area fits {name}'s own plan.

cards.prompt: Someday, your big celebration: a wedding, or whatever your version is. Your budget, your call. Pick the two that must happen.

options.t: Every relative there, even the ones I can't name.
The traditional ceremony, done properly, start to finish.
Something from my grandparents: a ring, a dish, a song.
Ten people max. The best dinner of our lives.
Most of the money goes to a trip or a home.
Something nobody's done: a hike, a game night, a beach.

cards.mask: looks like party planning; measures whether a big life moment should follow the ritual or your own design (R3, T21, T20)

cards.prompt: Your parents want you to keep helping an adult sibling who never quite gets it together. In that story, you're the…
cards.teenPrompt: Your sibling keeps needing a rescue: homework, chores, excuses. Your parents say, 'Help them, they're family.' In that story, you're the…

options.t: Safety net. I cover them, every single time.
Coach. I help once, then they learn it.
Deadline. 'Last time' comes with an actual date.
Grumbler. I help, then vent about it all week.
Secret sponsor. I help, and nobody else knows.
Referee. I tell my parents it's their call, not mine.

cards.mask: looks like a family cast list; measures whether your help to family is open-ended or has an end date (T18)

friend.prompt: {name}'s sibling keeps needing a rescue, and the parents say 'help, you're family.' {name} is the…

b.t: Deadline. Helps, with an end date.

cards.prompt: You and your person: solid, money sorted, plans shared. Does it still need a wedding to feel complete?

options.t: Yes. I want the vows, out loud, in front of people.
No. What we have is already the whole thing.

cards.mask: looks like a marriage hot take; measures whether commitment needs the classic ritual to count (R3, T21)

cards.prompt: The big family holiday. Someone suggests skipping the usual dinner this year and doing something totally different.

options.t: Absolutely not. Same dishes, same seats, same fight.
Yes! Hotpot on the roof, then a movie marathon.
Keep the one dish that matters. Reinvent the rest.
Do both: classic dinner first, the new thing after.

cards.mask: looks like holiday planning; measures whether tradition is the point or a starting draft (R3, T20); teen-safe R3 check

cards.prompt: Your family starts a weekly Sunday dinner. Attendance is 'optional', said in a voice that means it isn't.

options.t: Never miss one. I'm on dessert duty.
Show up most weeks, gone by eight.
Pitch once a month instead. Weekly is a lot.
Show up and turn it into game night.
Skip it, but call a different relative each week.

cards.mask: looks like a dinner invite; measures how much shared family time feels like home versus a lot (R1, T19)
